chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the waiting period of the woman who undergoes khul' (divorce by redemption), how long is it? He said: 'The waiting period of the divorced woman, and she should observe it in her house, and the woman who undergoes mubarat (mutual divorce) is in the same status as the woman who undergoes khul'.'

key_terms.الْمُبَارِئَةُ: The woman who undergoes mubarat (mutual divorce)
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةِ: The woman who undergoes khul' (divorce by redemption)
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: In the status of / equivalent to

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman who undergoes khul' or mubarat divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Tahdhib, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah, clarifies that the 'iddah for khul' and mubarat mirrors that of a standard talaq, emphasizing the domestic setting for this period. In Shia jurisprudence, this equality underscores that the primary purpose of 'iddah—ensuring paternity certainty and allowing for reconciliation—remains consistent regardless of whether the divorce is initiated by the husband or wife. The ruling highlights the legal parity between these forms of dissolution, reinforcing the stability of the family unit during the transition.
